who: Svatmarama · Hatha Yoga Pradipika 1.66 (tr. Pancham Sinh)
quote: Whether young, old or too old, sick or lean, one who discards laziness, gets success if he practises Yoga.
meaning: Young or old, sick or weak, anyone who stops being lazy and keeps practicing yoga will succeed.

quote: My brothers and sister had learned to swim in four or five lessons, but eighteen were required for me.
meaning: Annette wore steel leg braces as a small child. Swimming slowly made her legs strong, and by 1902 she was a champion.

quote: The drop hollows out the stone; the ring is worn by use.
meaning: A soft drop of water, falling again and again, can wear a hole in hard stone.

who: Martha Graham · This I Believe, c. 1953
quote: It takes about 10 years to make a mature dancer... The body is shaped, disciplined, honored and in time, trusted.
meaning: Martha Graham began serious dance training at 22 in 1916, late for a dancer, and went on to make 181 dances.

quote: There is nothing which practice cannot make easy; so by practice in slight sufferings we learn to bear great pains.
meaning: Practice small hard things every day. Bit by bit, you grow strong enough to carry the big ones.

who: Johnny Weissmuller · Swimming the American Crawl, 1930
quote: I had to do my stuff every day, whether anybody was looking or not.
meaning: A skinny, awkward boy with a poor stroke in 1920, he trained daily and won five Olympic golds by 1928.

quote: ...the mind is hard to curb and restless; but it may be curbed by constant practice and by dispassion.
meaning: The mind is restless and hard to hold. But steady practice, day after day, can train it.

quote: I feel sure that it was this training which has enabled me to do whatever I have done in science.
meaning: Darwin's teachers thought him 'a very ordinary boy.' Daily focus on a five-year sea voyage from 1831 made him a great scientist.

quote: He who mixes with the experts while he is himself still stiff and imperfect... though he have not the natural talent for it, he will not lag far behind the others.
meaning: Stiff and new? Practice next to skilled people anyway. With time, you will not be far behind.

who: Vincent van Gogh · Letter to Theo, 1880
quote: ...my pencil has become somewhat obedient and seems to become more so day by day.
meaning: In 1880 he was broke and sad. He kept drawing every day. In ten years he made over 800 paintings.
